html:
Omar Mukhtar was a teacher of the Quran in the Senussi order who led the armed resistance to Italian rule in Cyrenaica for nearly twenty years. He was hanged by the Italians in September 1931.

From the 1920s, already in his sixties, he led small bands of horsemen in the hills of the Jebel Akhdar, striking Italian columns and slipping away. To cut his fighters off, the Italians under General Graziani forced the people of Cyrenaica into camps and fenced the Egyptian border.

He was wounded, captured and, after a quick trial, hanged at Suluq before thousands of interned people. He became the national hero of Libya, his face on its money, and the subject of the film Lion of the Desert (1981). See also Italy's invasion.
